premises.name: Full arbitrary-rank/sign Gaussian-mixture QFORM theorem
premises.scope: Independent Gaussian location-scale-mixture coordinates with E[T_i^(-1/2)]<=sqrt(2*pi); arbitrary symmetric A and affine terms.

premises.name: Scale-covariant physical-three-coordinate Schur localization
premises.scope: Physical invertible 3x3 principal block; density bound 6 sqrt(pi)/sigma with zero support/tail/translation tax.

result.statement: For a Gaussian location-scale mixture g with M=E[T^(-1/2)], Var(g)<=sqrt(2/pi)M. Therefore the normalized Gaussian-mixture class M<=sqrt(2*pi) and all its weak limits have BV<=2. An admissible cap-one N-fragment indicator has BV=2N and any weak Gaussian-mixture approximation requires liminf M>=N sqrt(2*pi). Moreover, for separated gaps L, every cap-one density g with Var(g)<=V satisfies ||f_NL-g||_1 >= (2N-V)/(N+1/L).
result.partner_application: For B_*=I_3-(2/3)11^T, spec {1,1,-1}, and the fragmented inputs, account04/B14 gives ||p_{X^T B_* X}||_infty,ess <= 6 sqrt(pi).

unresolved_implication: The unrestricted rough-input QFORM theorem cannot be obtained by constant-preserving per-coordinate localization to the checked normalized Gaussian-mixture class. A proof must average/group rough fragments jointly with matrix geometry or use another localization/receiver.
next_step: Seek a product-preserving grouped localization whose control parameter is insensitive to one-dimensional BV/fragment count, and test it on the diffuse bank families where every physical triple degenerates.
